chapter: Bands, leaders and radio of the thirties and forties
title: Forties and fifties radio: Merry Macs, Peter Van Steeden and Fred Allen
summary: Having become an outside man who took any work, he played vibes with the Merry Macs and for seven years on the Fred Allen show with Peter Van Steeden.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Okay. Then after him, Casper Reardon, you spent the next 20 years as an outside man.
As an outside man, yes.
What is an outside man?
An outside man is a man who takes anything that comes his way.
I see, okay. And what came your way? What did you do mostly? During the forties, what kind of work did you do mostly?
During the forties?
Uh huh. After Leith Stevens and after the Saturday Night Swing Club and Casper Reardon, what kind of work did you do?
I did any work that they told me to do.
Like what?
Well like...
Do you recall playing the vibraphone behind the Merry Macs on the Fred Allen show and on their Decca recordings?
Sure, that's right.
And Carl Kress was a member of it. And his wife was one of the singers at that time, with the McMichael Brothers.
That's where he became good friends with Carl Kress.
Yeah.
I think they lived near one another.
Yes. Do you remember Pete Van Steeden?
Pete Van Steeden?
Peter Van Steeden.
Do you remember him? You worked for him for three years I think.
Yeah.
And he started the Fred Allen show.
Yeah.

He was the band leader on the Fred Allen show and somewhere in Chauncey's collection apparently - Peter Van Steeden has had a leg amputated. And when he heard about Chauncey, he's sending me a card saying he knew, he had gone through the same procedure.
That band at the Fred Allen show that he had, he formed that from the old Lennie Hayton band. Do you remember that?
Which?
The Fred Allen band.
The Fred Allen band, the old...
That was the nucleus of the Lennie Hayton orchestra.
Oh I see.
Do you remember that? You don't remember that. Okay. And then you did Fred Allen for seven years.
Yeah.
That was the entire run of the show. And then you did some other radio programs. Do you remember those?
No.
Some other radio programs. Let' see - The $64,000 Question.
The $64,000 question?
Do you remember that?
No.
You did that. I think you did.
